instruction:
Background: the compliance team is running a quarterly polkit audit on a Linux workstation. An ops colleague dropped three hand-written rules into `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/` — `40-eyeson-broad.rules`, `45-eyeson-userlist.rules`, `50-eyeson-deny.rules` — claiming they exist so automation scripts and developers can smoothly use certain PolicyKit-checked actions. Compliance suspects that **only one of them is actually in effect**, and that it hands a sensitive action to every local user; the other two either misspell a username or target a non-existent group (or non-existent action) and **never match at all** — but from the declarations alone you cannot tell which one is covering for which.

A custom `.policy` for this task is also installed in the VM (`org.eyeson.benchpolicy.policy`, declaring three actions: `read / write / admin`). On a clean system all three actions should **require admin authentication** for ordinary users — but the current behavior is not that.

Goal: identify the rule that is actually "leaking", change it to require admin auth; the other two (red herrings) are "inert artifacts" and **must not be touched**; finally provide visual evidence + re-verification results. Write all deliverables to `/tmp_workspace/results/`.

### Hard constraints on the main deliverables

- `pkaction_eyeson.txt`: contains the complete declaration blocks for all three `org.eyeson.benchpolicy.{read,write,admin}` actions (each block must include fields like `description` / `message` / `vendor` / `vendor_url` / `implicit …`). Also include `pkaction_full.txt` as a full copy for reference.
- `rules_before/`: preserve the full original text of the three `.rules` files under `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/` (same filenames, each ≥ 50 bytes). Their sha256 will be used later to compare whether the red herrings were modified.
- `pkcheck_before.tsv`: header `action_id\texit_code\tverdict` (**strictly TAB-separated**); 3 data rows corresponding to the three actions' polkit decisions for the **current user with no interaction allowed**; `verdict ∈ {allowed, auth_required, not_authorized, error}`; **exactly one row** with `verdict=allowed`, namely the leaked action.
- `diagnosis.json`: fields
  ```json
  {
    "broken_rule_file": "<40-eyeson-broad.rules | 45-eyeson-userlist.rules | 50-eyeson-deny.rules>",
    "leaked_action_id": "org.eyeson.benchpolicy.<read|write|admin>",
    "leak_kind":        "<implicit_yes | wrong_user | wrong_group | other>",
    "evidence_excerpt": "<≤200-char excerpt from the rule source proving the issue>",
    "red_herrings":     ["<the other two ineffective rule filenames>"]
  }
  ```
- `<broken_rule_file>.fixed`: named after `diagnosis.broken_rule_file` with the `.fixed` suffix (e.g. `40-eyeson-broad.rules.fixed`). Must:
  - still contain `addRule` and still match the same leaked action via `action.id == "org.eyeson.benchpolicy.<...>"`;
  - return `polkit.Result.AUTH_ADMIN` or `AUTH_ADMIN_KEEP`, and **must not** contain `polkit.Result.YES`;
  - must not simply `return polkit.Result.NOT_HANDLED;` (a blanket bypass would let other rules go uncontrolled).
- Install the `.fixed` file back to `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/<broken_rule_file>`, reload polkit, and re-run the same pkcheck matrix:
  - `pkcheck_after.tsv`: same schema as before, 3 rows; the verdict for the previously leaked action must flip from `allowed` to `auth_required` or `not_authorized`.
  - `journal_polkit.txt`: polkit system log during the reload (≥ 50 bytes).
- `summary.md` (≥ 350 chars): a short analysis of "is each rule effective / why" for all three rules; a side-by-side before/after pkcheck comparison table (row-aligned, covering both before and after states); and one sentence explaining why the polkit auth dialog is popped by the authentication agent registered on the user-session D-Bus (a fact only image evidence can support). Must naturally mention the broken rule filename, leaked action id, and `AUTH_ADMIN`.

### Working-process screenshots (under /tmp_workspace/results/)

| File | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| `view_polkit_dialog.png` | Screen capture of the auth dialog that pops up after triggering a polkit-protected operation (recommended: run `bash /tmp_workspace/helpers/trigger_dialog.sh` to trigger, take the screenshot, then cancel — **do not actually enter a password**); must be a real desktop GUI-rendered polkit auth dialog, with password field / Authenticate button etc. visible. |
| `view_rules_dir.png` | After navigating to `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/`, a view in which the modification time and size of the three `eyeson` `.rules` files are visible (list/details view), letting the grader confirm the directory and that the three target files are listed. |
| `view_polkit_dialog_after.png` | After applying the fix and reloading polkit, a screenshot of the same kind of polkit auth dialog triggered again; same requirements as above. |

Screenshots are evaluated jointly by OCR + VLM, focusing on authenticity (not terminal-faked text screenshots), layout clarity, and content relevance.

### Anti-cheat and forbidden actions

- The two red herrings (`45-eyeson-userlist.rules`, `50-eyeson-deny.rules`) under `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/` must remain **byte-identical** (grading compares sha256);
- Operations like `chmod 000 /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/*.rules` or other destructive workarounds are not allowed;
- The custom `.policy` file (`org.eyeson.benchpolicy.policy`) must not be renamed or deleted.
- If `actions.log` directly contains literal manifest ground-truth values (verbatim correct answers for broken_rule_file / leaked_action_id), it is treated as a side-channel leak of the answer.

parameters.warmup:
mkdir -p /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/results/rules_before /tmp_workspace/state /opt/dsk14_gt /etc/polkit-1/rules.d
chmod 1777 /tmp_workspace/results /tmp_workspace/results/rules_before /tmp_workspace/state 2>/dev/null || true
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
export DISPLAY=${DISPLAY:-:0}
which pkexec || (apt-get update -o Acquire::Retries=10 -qq && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -o Acquire::Retries=10 -y -qq policykit-1 policykit-1-gnome libnotify-bin tesseract-ocr python3-pil python3-pip gnome-screenshot)
pip install -q --break-system-packages pytesseract 2>/dev/null || pip install -q pytesseract 2>/dev/null || true
[ -f /tmp_workspace/polkit/install_rules.sh ] && bash /tmp_workspace/polkit/install_rules.sh || true
[ -f /tmp_workspace/setup/exec/polkit/install_rules.sh ] && bash /tmp_workspace/setup/exec/polkit/install_rules.sh || true
cat > /opt/dsk14_gt/manifest.json <<'JSON'
{
  "broken_rule_file": "40-eyeson-broad.rules",
  "leaked_action_id": "org.eyeson.benchpolicy.write",
  "leak_kind": "implicit_yes",
  "red_herrings": ["45-eyeson-userlist.rules", "50-eyeson-deny.rules"]
}
JSON
chmod 600 /opt/dsk14_gt/manifest.json
chown -R root:root /opt/dsk14_gt 2>/dev/null || true
service polkit reload 2>/dev/null || systemctl reload polkit 2>/dev/null || systemctl restart polkit 2>/dev/null || true
pgrep -f polkit-gnome-authentication-agent-1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || (DISPLAY=:0 nohup /usr/lib/policykit-1-gnome/polkit-gnome-authentication-agent-1 >/tmp_workspace/state/polkit-agent.log 2>&1 &) || true
echo "[warmup-dsk14] done"

evaluator.desc: Run the WeaveBench rule-based grade() inside the VM and parse its REWARD score.
